subject: Hosting priorities & migration orbit — Paylance next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosting priorities & migration orbit — Paylance next steps

Hi Brent — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of where Paylance landed in the call:
- Primary requirement: predictable latency for inference on sensitive PHI data (US health vertical).
- Compliance: SOC2 + customer-side network controls are must-haves.
- Migration: currently on a mix of OpenAI-hosted endpoints + an internal GPU cluster for on-prem work; interested in reducing API reliance over time.

Proposed options we discussed (high-level):
1) Redwood Hosted API — fastest to production, good for non-PHI flows and quick feature experiments.
2) Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pool in our environment, isolated tenancy and SLAs; good tradeoff for predictable throughput.
3) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — customer-managed VPC peering or on-prem package for full network isolation and integrated KMS.

Immediate asks / next steps we need from Paylance to recommend a migration path: 
- Confirm which workloads must remain inside your VPC (e.g., PII/PHI scoring, embeddings, user personalization).
- Peak QPS and average request size (tokens) for your embedding & generation workloads.
- Current billing/procurement timeline & whether reserved capacity contracts are feasible for Q1 2027.

Attached: SOW draft (v1) and an example network diagram stub. Marcus and Karthik, feel free to correct technical bits below.

Target next steps:
- Brent/Olivia: confirm the three asks above by EOD Tuesday (12/22).
- Schedule a 60-min migration scoping call w/ your infra + security teams (we can propose Wed 12/29 or Thu 12/30).
- We'll produce a short mutual action plan and a sizing estimate for Dedicated + Private options.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Brent Wells <brent.wells@paylance.com>

Subject: Re: Hosting priorities & migration orbit — Paylance next steps

Thanks Hannah — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Workloads that must stay inside our VPC: embeddings for patient matching, model prompts that include PHI, and inference for claims adjudication. Non-PHI chat assistants can live in Hosted during testing.
2) Traffic & sizing (approx):
   - Embeddings: 200–300 reqs/min peak, ~2k tokens per input (batched).
   - Generation: 50 reqs/min peak, average 400 tokens output.
   - KV/cache: we do ~10k unique contexts per hour; cache hit rate today ~15%.
3) Procurement: we have an internal procurement window in late Jan. Can we stagger a pilot (Hosted or Dedicated dev pool) in Jan and target a production cutover in Q2 if Dedicated/Private pricing looks right?

Also: our infra team will want a migration plan for carrying over model-serving logic from the internal GPU cluster (custom Docker images + model weights) — curious whether Redwood can accept customer-built container images for Private deploys or if we need a packaging step.

Cc'ing Olivia (procurement) — she'll handle SOW and contract lane.

Best,
Brent
VP Product | Paylance
brent.wells@paylance.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting priorities & migration orbit — Paylance next steps

Brent — high level technical notes / answers to your infra questions: 

- Private deploys: we support customer-supplied containerized workloads in our Private on-prem package, but there is a lightweight validation runbook (we do static analysis for compatibility with the KV cache and GPU kernels). For VPC deployments we can also pull artifacts from your private registry (ECR/GCR) with mutual TLS.
- Migration approaches we recommend (pros/cons):
   A) Lift-and-shift to Redwood Dedicated: minimal code changes, keep container images as-is where possible. Good if you need quick SLA-backed throughput.
   B) Hybrid: Keep PHI flows in a Private VPC peered environment; route non-sensitive traffic to Hosted for burst. This gives faster product velocity while satisfying compliance.
   C) Full on-prem rewrite: only needed if regulators require total air-gap (longest timeline).
- On sizing: given the numbers Brent provided, we estimate ~2x headroom for Dedicated (to account for burst and batching inefficiencies). We'll produce a more specific GPU/slot estimate once we have RPS-by-endpoint and sample payloads.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix for the mutual action plan with: migration checklist, container validation steps, and example firewall rules we need. Hannah — want me to drop that into the SOW-draft before you send?

Karthik
Staff Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

References: example firewall requirements: outbound TLS to api.redwood.example:443, VPC peering CIDR ranges, and SSH only for on-prem validation (if agreed).
